blocks.content:
• Addresses State Legislature
• Nominates members of Legislative Council (if present)
• Gives assent to bills
• Can return non‑money bills once
• Can promulgate ordinances (Article 213)

rows: Can be returned once for reconsideration

items: Article 213 is frequently tested as the constitutional provision for the Governor's ordinance-making power.
Note that the Governor can return non-money bills only ONCE; money bills cannot be returned for reconsideration.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Addresses the State Legislature and nominates members to the Legislative Council if present.
Grants official assent to bills passed by the state legislature.
Possesses the authority to return non-money bills once for reconsideration.
Holds the constitutional power to promulgate ordinances under Article 213.
